root_cause.text: The RISC-V IOMMU invalidation code in `riscv_iommu_iotlb_inval()` used overflow-prone unsigned arithmetic (`end - start + 1` and `for (iova = start; iova < end; iova += PAGE_SIZE)`) on address ranges, so a valid `end == ULONG_MAX` range could wrap `iova` and loop indefinitely.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says “it should support a gather->end of ULONG_MAX, but if this happens it will infinite loop because of the overflow,” and the patch removes `unsigned long len = end - start + 1`, changes the range test to `end - start < RISCV_IOMMU_IOTLB_INVAL_LIMIT - 1`, and replaces `iova += PAGE_SIZE` with `check_add_overflow(iova, PAGE_SIZE, &iova)`.

intent_record.what: Two local variable declarations, `unsigned long len = end - start + 1;` and `unsigned long iova;`, were removed from `riscv_iommu_iotlb_inval()` while the surrounding logic shown in the hunk was left unchanged.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix per-page IOTLB invalidation to use a safe range check and overflow-protected address iteration.
intent_record.what: The range invalidation condition was changed from `if (len && len < RISCV_IOMMU_IOTLB_INVAL_LIMIT)` to `if (end - start < RISCV_IOMMU_IOTLB_INVAL_LIMIT - 1)`, the `for (iova = start; iova < end; iova += PAGE_SIZE)` loop was replaced with a block-local `unsigned long iova = start;` and a `do { ... } while (...)` loop, and the loop increment now uses `check_add_overflow(iova, PAGE_SIZE, &iova)` to stop on address overflow before continuing while `iova < end`.
intent_record.how: This changes small-range IOTLB invalidation to iterate safely over page addresses starting from `start` even without relying on `len`, and prevents unsigned address wraparound when advancing `iova` by `PAGE_SIZE`. At runtime, it avoids incorrect looping or invalidation behavior near the end of the address space while still sending per-page invalidation commands for bounded ranges and falling back to a broader invalidation for larger ranges.
